verses.1: And Rehoboam was king, son of Solomon. He ruled under King Nebukadnezar, who had ruled in Judah.
verses.2: And he did not listen to his servants and the people of the land regarding the words of Jehovah, which Jehovah spoke through the prophet Jeremiah.
verses.3: And King Zedekiah sent Jehoshaphat, son of Shemaiah, and Zadok, son of Merai, as priests to Jeremiah, the prophet, with these words: “Pray to the LORD our God for us.”
verses.4: And Jirmiyah came out among the people. But they did not give him a place in the house of the king.
verses.5: And Pharaoh’s army departed from Egypt. The enemies heard about Jerusalem’s fall, and they rushed up against it.
verses.6: And the words of Jehovah were spoken to the prophet Jeremiah, as follows:
verses.7: As the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Thus shall you say to the king of Judah, who has sent you to me to seek my counsel. Now, behold, the army of Pharaoh, which came to help you, has returned to Egypt.
verses.8: And the enemies returned, and they fought against this city. They burned it with fire.
verses.9: So said Yahweh: “Do not lift your spirits up, saying, ‘They will go away from us.’ For they will not really go away.”
verses.10: For if all the armies of those who fight against you were to be destroyed, and if only a few people remained alive, then those people would rise up from their shelters and burn down this city with fire.
verses.11: And when the army of the Assyrians rose up from above Jerusalem, they were defeated by Pharaoh’s army.
verses.12: And Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benyamin, so that he could divide it among the people.
verses.13: And he was in the gate of Benyamin. There, a man named Yerimya, son of Semeiah, son of Hananiah, confronted the prophet Yerimya and said, “You will fall.”
verses.14: And Jeremiah said, “He is a liar. I will not fall for his lies.” But Jeremiah did not listen to him. Then Jeremiah seized Jeremiah and brought him before the priests.
verses.15: And the priests angered themselves at Jeremiah. They beat him, and they handed him over to the house of Esau, that is, to Jehovah Nathan the scribe, as they wanted to make of him a “house of destruction.”
verses.16: For Jeremiah went into the temple and into the storage areas. There, Jeremiah stayed for many days.
verses.17: And the king sent Zadkiah to him. The king took him into his house and questioned him in a secret room. He said, “There is something from Jehovah.” Zadkiah replied, “Yes, there is.” Then the king said, “Give it to King Babylon.”
verses.18: And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What sins have I committed against you, your servants, and this people? Why did you bring me before the court of judgment?”
verses.19: And who is your prophet, that he might come to you and say, “A king will not come over you and over this land.”
verses.20: And now, O Lord king, please let me rest in your presence. Do not keep me in the house of Jehonatan the scribe. It is not true that I will be kept there.
verses.21: And King Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be taken into the palace. They placed him in the courtyard of the palace. They gave him some bread to eat, for the day was approaching when all the food in the city would be gone. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the palace.
